Subject: Post-demo recap & recommended next steps (VPC / Dedicated)

Thanks for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we don't lose momentum: 

Key notes from discovery:
- Production latency sensitivity for authorization flows (p95 target <= 80ms).
- Data residency and tenant isolation are blockers for procurement — Finly needs customer data to remain in your VPC.
- Expected volume: ~120k tokens/day today, unblock growth to ~1M tokens/day in 6 months.
- Procurement window aiming for Q3 decision, security review starts mid-May.

Recommended approach: Redwood Dedicated in VPC mode (private control plane + customer VPC peering)
- Preserves data residency and keeps logs in your network boundary.
- Predictable reserved capacity to hit latency SLOs and unit economics.
- We can provide an eval deployment in your VPC for a 2-week hands-on trial (no production traffic).

Immediate next steps (what I can action this week):
1) Share a deployment outline & sample network topology (attached: redwood-vpc-deployment-outline.pdf).
2) Drop SOC 2 summary and security checklist for your review (attached: SOC2-summary.pdf).
3) Rough committed quote for Dedicated capacity to cover expected scale (attached: estimated-dedicated-quote.xlsx).
4) Coordinate a short technical workshop with Rishi to walk infra + peering details (I can get on a 30-min slot next week).

Ask: Can you share the security reviewer contact and preferred time window next week for the workshop? If Priya wants to include an internal infra person, we can push calendar invites out.

I'll hold a placeholder for an eval slot the week of May 18 if that helps.

Best,
Connor O'Brien

Thanks Connor — helpful recap. A few clarifying questions from our side:

1) Timeline: our security review kicks off May 20 and procurement would like a decision by end of June. Is that timeline realistic for a Dedicated + VPC rollout if we opt for a small pilot?
2) Network: can the peering/topology support a NATed outbound pattern (our infra team is wary of changing inbound policies)? Any gotchas we should be aware of?
3) SLA / uptime: can you share a short example SLA for Dedicated customers? Also curious about backup/retention for logs (we can't forward logs to a third party).
4) Cost: the attached quote looks heavier than we expected. Do you have a break-even for burst vs reserved?

Looping in Priya (engineering lead) — Priya, assigning you for security and infra questions. If useful, we can have Rishi and our infra lead on a tech call next week.

—Alex

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & recommended next steps (VPC / Dedicated)

Appreciate the quick follow-up, Alex. Answers inline and a proposed plan: 

1) Timeline: Yes — a pilot can be stood up inside a week once we have network access and an approved PO. The typical flow: security review (1–2 weeks) -> test/proof-of-concept (2 weeks) -> procurement sign-off. Given your May 20 start, a June decision is reasonable.

2) Network topology: We support both inbound peering and outbound-only NAT egress patterns. Most customers use VPC peering with a small set of inbound rules; if you prefer outbound-only, we can run an egress-mode topology (details in attached network-playbook.md). No firewall rule changes are required on your inbound plane for egress-only.

3) SLA / retention: I'll attach a short SLA excerpt and can push our enterprise SLA doc if procurement needs it. Logs: we support pushing logs to your Kinesis/S3 endpoints inside the VPC — nothing leaves your account unless explicitly configured. (See SOC2-summary.pdf for attestations.)

4) Cost options: The quote includes a reserved baseline to guarantee p95 latency targets. We can propose a mixed model: smaller reserved commitment + burst pool for the first quarter to reduce upfront cost. I noted a few line items in estimated-dedicated-quote.xlsx that we can flex.

Proposed next step: schedule a 30-min technical workshop with Rishi and your infra lead to validate topology and exchange security contacts. Slot link: https://cal.com/redwood/30min?slot=2026-05-19

If you'd like, we can also provision a temporary eval tenant in your VPC for two weeks so your security team can run scans without impacting production.

Best,
Connor
